comment: Test pool machines (tools/remote/pool.mjs, docs/worktrees.md 'Test pool'). Override per machine with the "pool" key of the gitignored lf.local.json. A machine with "lanes" runs tests and sessions apart: the session lane is the server-2001 lock on UDP 2001 (sessions, host, serve; clients join it), each test lane is its own server-test-<k> lock with a server on 127.0.0.1:2001+k (-addr). Without "lanes" a machine keeps one shared lane of "slots" servers on 2001. sessionIdleMin (3): a session idle this long while a job waits is closed (a pool machine's sessions too, judged from this PC); sessionIdleMaxMin (5): one idle this long is closed with nobody waiting; any harness or session command resets the idle clock (sessions flow like a river: a lane is held for the window it is used). roomyMb (6144): RAM headroom past which a machine counts as roomy; a job goes to the machine with the most headroom after its reserve, weighted by speed (budgetMultiplier), and a machine below minFreeMb plus the reserve takes no job while another has room. promoteMin: a queued job moves up one priority level per this many minutes. minFreeMb: every server start, the first on a machine too, leaves this much RAM free after its reserve. sessionReserve: memory a second session reserves per profile (server MB plus MB per client; the full profile uses the sessionReserveServerMb/ClientMb defaults 600/850; measured 2026-11-10, docs/worktrees.md 'Session profiles'). bootBudgetS: a server not ready by then is killed (exit 124). A machine's budgetMultiplier scales the seeded run budgets and the boot budget (the laptop is about 2x slower). sessionHoldMin: a session started after the cap existed that is older than this while another session request queues is warned, then closed sessionGraceMin later (session up --hold <min> raises its own, to sessionHoldMaxMin); with nobody queued there is no cap. Lanes are ceilings (ports and heat); what starts is decided live per machine: a job must fit the machine's free RAM (read live, here and over ssh for a pool machine), a session reserves its server and clients, and beside other servers it must also leave minFreeMb. A RAM change needs no edit here. lf-testbox (ROG Zephyrus G15, Ryzen 9 6900HS, RTX 3070 Ti, 15.6 GB RAM since 2026-11-14, was 47 GB): 2026-11-14 it had 3.8-4.2 GB free with nothing of the pool running (the user desktop, Steam, a Workbench), and it powered itself off (ASUS thermal protection) 0-5 min after pool bursts, sitting at 93 C with 2 servers and 4 clients. Since the same day it stands outside (53-60 C idle) and runs up to 2 session lanes of at most 2 clients each (maxClients) and 3 test lanes, as RAM allows; it holds new jobs while the newest reading of its thermal logger (thermalLog, CSV with a thrm_c column, fresh within 2 min) is at or over thermalHoldC.
